draft.title: Aboriginal customary lore
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have their own systems of lore. Lore is passed down through generations, in stories, songs, ceremony and teaching from Elders.
This lore has been in place for thousands of years, long before the British legal system came to Australia. Each community has its own lore, so it is not the same everywhere.
Lore guides how people behave and how they relate to each other. It also guides the responsibilities people have to look after Country, which includes land, waters, plants and animals.
Customary lore is not the same as statute law made by parliament. Many communities continue to follow their lore today, alongside Australian law.
draft.remember: Lore is a living system of rules passed down over thousands of years. It guides behaviour and care for Country.

a.q: Which of these best describes Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander customary lore?
opts: Rules for behaviour and Country, passed down by Elders
Laws written by parliament for Aboriginal communities
Decisions made by judges that set later precedents
A single set of rules that is the same for every community
a.why: Lore is passed down through generations and guides behaviour and relationships with Country. It is not made by parliament or judges, and each community has its own lore, so it is not one shared set of rules.
a.clue: Think about how lore is shared and how long it has existed.

b.q: Uncle Ray, an Elder, teaches young people in his community how to care for a river and the animals that live there, using stories handed down from his grandparents. What is he passing on?
opts: Customary lore about responsibilities to Country
Common law built from the precedents of judges
Statute law passed by the NSW Parliament
Civil law used to settle a dispute over a contract
b.why: Stories handed down by Elders that guide care for the river and its animals are customary lore, which includes responsibilities to Country. Statute law is made by parliament and common law by judges, so neither fits this case.
b.clue: Who is teaching, and what is being passed down?

a.best: Rules for behaviour and Country, passed down by Elders

b.best: Customary lore about responsibilities to Country
